title: Kwame's idea won the Triborough pitch. Chad Kensington thinks it was yours and offers you the lead.

options.label: Tell Chad it was Kwame's
options.cost: The lead and a C$1,500 bonus

outcomes.text: Chad blinks, then gives Kwame the lead. Kwame mouths 'I owe you.' Half the floor saw what you did.

later.text: Remember the pitch you gave back? Kwame's startup just got funded. He made you a founding partner, and his post naming you is everywhere.
later.headline: Developing: newly funded founder Kwame names {name} as 'the reason I'm here.' Insiders say {name} once handed back a whole promotion.

outcomes.text: Chad shrugs: 'Fine, Kwame leads.' Kwame takes the bonus and forgets your name by Friday.

options.label: Take the lead
options.get: The lead and a C$1,500 bonus
options.cost: Kwame, who sits next to you

outcomes.text: You take the lead and the bonus. Kwame says nothing. He keeps saying nothing, very loudly, every day.

later.text: Remember Kwame's pitch? He kept the timestamps. He's asking you, in front of everyone, to set the record straight.

outcomes.text: You take the lead. Kwame quits a week later for a rival firm. Nobody connects it. Yet.

options.label: Call it a team effort
options.riskWhy: 'Team' is doing a lot of work

outcomes.text: 'Honestly? Team effort.' Chad splits the bonus. Kwame smiles like someone counting.

title: Kwame emailed the original pitch deck, timestamps and all, to the whole floor. Everyone's looking at you.

options.label: Admit it, out loud
options.cost: The lead, the bonus, the floor's respect
options.riskWhy: Apologies are long in this office

outcomes.text: You stand up and say it. Chad takes back the bonus and the lead. Kwame, weirdly, shakes your hand. Day one of the long way back.
You call it doctored. Half the floor believes you. Kwame's cousin, a lawyer, doesn't.

later.text: Remember calling Kwame's deck a fake? IT pulled the server logs. Chad walked you out holding your desk plant.
later.headline: BREAKING: {name} walked out of Triborough Works holding a desk plant after server logs backed a coworker's claim. We reached out. The plant declined to comment.

outcomes.text: You call it doctored. Kwame shrugs and leaves for a rival. The lead is yours, and so is the silence at lunch.
He takes the C$750 and deletes the email. You both have to live with lunch now.
He forwards your offer to Chad: 'They tried to buy me.' Fantastic.

title: Sharm hummed the hook that became Real Clout FM's new jingle. The station credits you and wants you on air.

options.label: Tell them it was Sharm's
options.riskWhy: Radio people talk to each other

outcomes.text: 'It was Sharm's.' The producer gives Sharm the credit. Sharm gives you a key to the booth and a standing invite.

later.text: Remember giving Sharm the jingle credit? Sharm got a second show and made you the weekly guest.

options.label: Take the credit
options.get: On air tonight, a C$1,200 fee
options.cost: Sharm hears it on her own station

outcomes.text: You do the segment. C$1,200. Sharm turns her studio speakers off when you walk by.
You do the segment. C$1,200. Sharm plays her original voice memo on The Wake-Up Call the next morning.

later.text: Remember the jingle? Sharm's voice memo from March went around. The station dropped your segment and is 'reviewing how it credits people.'
later.headline: Developing: Real Clout FM drops {name}'s segment after a voice memo shows the station jingle was hummed by its own morning DJ. We're told the jingle stays.

outcomes.text: You pitch a duo. The producer says 'cute' and books it. C$600 each and a running bit.
The producer wanted one face, and now it's neither of yours.

title: Mags slides you one wristband for Peyton Pastel's VIP room. Just one. Ana paid for your ride here.

options.label: Go in without Ana
options.get: Peyton's VIP room, maybe her story

outcomes.text: Peyton tags you in her story. 40,000 people see your face. Ana sees it too, from the bus.

later.text: Remember leaving Ana at the bar? She posted the night from her side: 'Love that for you.' The comments picked a side, and it wasn't yours.

outcomes.text: Inside, Peyton never looks at you. You take selfies near her for an hour. Ana's not answering.
You and Ana dance by the speakers and roast every outfit going into VIP. Best night of the month.

later.text: Remember skipping Peyton's VIP room for Ana? Ana's cousin casts for Clout TV. She asked for you by name.

options.label: Get Ana in the back way

outcomes.text: The service corridor works. You're both in, and in the back of Peyton's photos all night.
Mags is at the service door. 'Seriously?' You're both off the list. Every list.

title: Kiki's list for Lunaria's rooftop afterparty has your name. Not Dee's. Dee is mid-sentence.

outcomes.text: Lunaria asks your name twice and calls you 'the funny one.' It ends up in her caption.

later.text: Remember leaving Dee at the rooftop? Dee stopped inviting you. So did Dee's friends, who turned out to be most of your friends.

outcomes.text: Upstairs is six people staring at phones. Lunaria leaves in four minutes. Dee went home.
'We're good down here.' Dee notices. Dee tells everyone. People like hearing it.

later.text: Remember turning down Lunaria for Dee? Kiki told Lunaria's manager. 'Loyal people are rare.' You're invited to the next listening session.

outcomes.text: Kiki rolls her eyes, then waves you both up. Dee meets Lunaria. Dee will tell this story at your wedding.
'Then neither.' The rope stays closed. Dee hugs you anyway.

title: Chardonnay Shade sent you a drunk voice note by mistake: every castmate, ranked, rudely. Lola will pay.

options.label: Send it to Lola
options.riskWhy: Chardonnay can't keep a grudge quiet

outcomes.text: Lola runs it: 'EXCLUSIVE.' C$2,500 and your name on the tip. The cast isn't speaking to Chardonnay. Or you.

later.text: Remember the voice note? Chardonnay found out who sold it. She's here, with a camera crew.

outcomes.text: 'You DELETED it?' She's genuinely stunned. She saves your number as 'the honest one.'

later.text: Remember deleting Chardonnay's voice note? She put you on her spin-off. 'Everyone needs one person who doesn't sell them out.'
later.headline: Developing: Chardonnay Shade's spin-off adds {name}, called by Shade 'the only person in Queens who's never sold me out.' Filming starts soon, we're told.

outcomes.text: You file it in a folder called 'taxes.' It feels like carrying a lit match.
Weeks later Chardonnay asks, sweetly, if you got 'anything weird' from her. You say no. She knows.

title: Chardonnay Shade and a camera crew corner you: 'Did you sell my voice note?' The red light is on.

options.label: Admit it on camera
options.cost: Your face in a villain edit

outcomes.text: 'Yeah. I did. I'm sorry.' Chardonnay is speechless for the first time on camera. The episode makes you the honest villain.
You admit it. They score it with violins and a slow zoom. The comments are brutal for a week.
You deny it. Lola posts your email, the timestamp and the C$2,500. On camera, Chardonnay just points.
You deny it and she believes you. Her assistant takes the blame and is fired. You sleep fine. Mostly.

options.label: Lean in: 'Someone had to'
options.get: A villain era, and a following

outcomes.text: 'Someone had to tell the truth.' The clip goes huge. Producers love you. Velvet Static, where she drinks, doesn't.

title: Chase Clout left a private rehearsal on the arena's PC: an hour of him practicing his 'shocked' face.

outcomes.text: 'Chase Clout rehearses his surprise face' gets 3 million views. Your followers triple. So does your hate mail.

later.text: Remember the rehearsal clip? Chase's fans dug up your old posts. Pixel banned you from the arena 'to keep the peace.'

outcomes.text: The clip goes huge. Chase laughs it off on stream and calls you 'my biggest fan.' Somehow that's worse.
Pixel wipes the drive and comps your sessions for a month. 'You could have ended him. Weird flex not to.'

later.text: Remember not leaking Chase's rehearsal? Pixel told him. Chase had you co-stream the tournament final.

outcomes.text: Chase's manager sends C$2,000 and 'we never spoke.' You've never spoken. You're richer.
Chase reads your DM on stream: 'Chat, someone's trying to shake me down.' Chat is not on your side.

title: Chase Clout's manager: date Chase on camera for a month. C$2,500 and a million viewers. You've met him twice.

options.label: Sign the 'relationship'
options.cost: A month of fake love, then the breakup

outcomes.text: Your first 'date' trends. C$2,500. Chase calls you 'babe' on stream and forgets your name off it.

later.text: Remember dating Chase Clout 'for real'? The staged breakup aired. His edit made you the villain. His fans are thorough.
later.headline: BREAKING: Chase Clout and {name} split live on stream. Chase: 'I gave everything.' We're told the contract said thirty days.

outcomes.text: 'Pass.' The manager calls Tiff next. Tiff says yes before he finishes the sentence.
'Friends who game' gets C$800 and steady views. No fake tears needed.
The manager laughs and hangs up. Chase's next 'girlfriend' gets your slot.

title: Brock Squarejaw's publicist: leave the club on Brock's arm tonight. His divorce news drops tomorrow.

outcomes.text: The photos run everywhere: 'MYSTERY NEW YORKER.' You're the mystery. The publicist sends flowers and C$1,500.

later.text: Remember leaving Ultraviolet with Brock? His ex did a tell-all. You're 'the distraction.' Her fans are organized.
later.headline: Developing: Brock Squarejaw's ex names {name} as 'the distraction' in a tell-all. Sources say the two left a club together once, for eleven seconds.

outcomes.text: 'Nope.' The publicist finds someone at the bar in under a minute. You read the headlines at breakfast, unbothered.
Lola runs 'Brock's team staging photos tonight.' C$1,200. The publicist has you walked out the side door.

title: You knocked over the key light at the Clout TV shoot. Nour assumes it was Jae, the 19-year-old assistant.

options.label: Say it was you
options.cost: C$800 for the light, Nour's glare

outcomes.text: 'That was me.' You pay for the light. Nour stares, then writes something down.

later.text: Remember owning the light at Clout TV? Nour wrote 'trustworthy' next to your name. She's booking you for her next three shoots.

outcomes.text: Jae gets sent home in tears. You get rebooked: C$1,200 and a better slot.

later.text: Remember the light at Clout TV? The behind-the-scenes camera caught everything. Jae's mom posted it.
later.headline: BREAKING: behind-the-scenes footage shows {name} knocking over a light while a 19-year-old assistant took the fall. Clout TV is 'reviewing its talent list.'

outcomes.text: Jae gets fired. You get the slot. Nobody ever finds out. You do, every time you see an assistant.
You sweep up glass while Jae apologizes for something you did. Nour thanks you for helping. Ouch.

title: You came in late on your set. The booker heard the screech and is glaring at Teo, the sound guy.

outcomes.text: The booker shrugs: 'Happens.' Teo starts making you sound twice as good every set.

later.text: Remember owning your late entry? Teo mixed your set into a live tape. Real Clout FM won't stop playing it.

outcomes.text: The booker drops you from next month. Teo buys you a drink: 'Respect.'

options.label: Blame the monitors
options.riskWhy: Sound guys talk to every venue

outcomes.text: Teo's let go. You get the headline slot and C$1,500.

later.text: Remember blaming Teo's monitors? Every sound guy in Queens heard. Your next three sets sound like a fax machine.

options.label: Make it a bit on the mic

outcomes.text: 'That screech was the new single.' The room laughs. The booker laughs. Teo laughs loudest.
The joke dies. The booker blames Teo anyway, and you let it happen.

title: Tiff, who gave you your very first shoutout, wants a tag in your post. Your new followers find her 'cringe.'

outcomes.text: You tag her. 300 people unfollow. Tiff cries in your DMs, the good kind.

later.text: Remember tagging Tiff when it cost you? Her 'cringe' video blew up. She's tagging you in everything. 2 million views.

outcomes.text: You leave her on read. Your engagement goes up. Tiff posts 'some people forget.'

later.text: Remember leaving Tiff on read? Her 'some people forget' post had your old DMs in it. Everyone has a Tiff, and opinions.

options.label: Tag her in a story instead

outcomes.text: A story tag. Tiff reposts it 14 times. Nobody else notices. Fine.

title: DJ Polaroid, who gave you your first set, begs you to come to his empty 7 PM slot. Lunaria's party is tonight.

outcomes.text: You're one of four people there. You dance like it's sold out. Polaroid plays his best set ever, to you.

later.text: Remember the empty 7 PM set? Polaroid just landed a headline night. He wants you there.

outcomes.text: Lunaria's party is everything. Polaroid plays to an empty room, and posts a photo of it.

later.text: Remember skipping Polaroid's set? He's headlining now. Asked on the radio who stood by him, he listed everyone. Not you.

outcomes.text: You catch one song, hug him, and make Lunaria's by midnight. Everybody sort of wins.

title: DJ Polaroid's headlining and offers you the opening set. A bigger name will pay you C$3,000 to step aside.

outcomes.text: You open for Polaroid. The crowd is huge. He shouts your name on the mic like you're family.
C$3,000. Polaroid hears it from the big name, not from you. He doesn't call again.

options.label: Give it to a kid who needs it

outcomes.text: You hand it to a kid who DJs in a laundromat. Polaroid hugs you both. Lola writes it up.

title: At the door, a nervous kid in thrift-store clothes asks you to vouch for him. Your group is laughing.

options.label: Vouch for him
options.riskWhy: If he embarrasses you, you own it

outcomes.text: He gets in, dances badly and thanks you nine times. Your group calls you 'the charity.'

later.text: Remember vouching for the kid at Ultraviolet? He's Skyler Beta's little brother. Skyler sent a thank-you, with stock.

outcomes.text: He gets in and is sick on the bouncer's shoes. You're off the list for a week.
You laugh. He leaves. Your group buys you a drink. It tastes fine.

later.text: Remember laughing at the kid at Ultraviolet's door? He's a designer now. He told the story in a big interview and described your shoes.
later.headline: BREAKING: rising designer recalls being laughed at by {name} outside Ultraviolet Society. 'Their shoes were worse than mine,' he told us.

options.label: Point him to a friendlier spot

outcomes.text: 'Try The Sticky Floor, they're nicer.' He goes. He leaves a comment on your profile: '10/10 human.'

title: The popular table at the dining hall waves you over. The freshman you've sat with all week has no one else.

outcomes.text: You stay. He talks about frogs for an hour. You learn a lot about frogs.

later.text: Remember the freshman you sat with? He won student government by a landslide. Guess who he named his chief of staff.

outcomes.text: The popular table loves you. The freshman eats alone, and you see him eating alone all week.
They squeeze him in. He turns out to be hilarious. You're the one who found him.
'Oh, we meant just you.' You both sit back down. He saw the look.

title: A casting email for Tiff landed in your inbox by mistake: a Clout TV pilot. Callbacks are tomorrow.

outcomes.text: You forward it. Tiff books it and thanks you on camera in episode one.

later.text: Remember forwarding Tiff's casting email? She remembered. You're her plus-one to the premiere, on the carpet.

options.label: Go to the callback yourself
options.get: A shot at a TV pilot

outcomes.text: You show up: 'Tiff couldn't make it.' You get the part: C$2,000 and a recurring bit.

later.text: Remember 'Tiff couldn't make it'? Tiff asked casting why they never emailed her. They checked. Your reply is in the chain.
later.headline: Developing: Clout TV recasts a pilot role after learning {name} answered a casting email meant for someone else. Insiders call it 'bold.'

outcomes.text: You go in. They wanted Tiff's look, not yours. Nobody gets the part.
Deleted. Tiff never knows. The role goes to someone neither of you has heard of.

title: A sneaker brand wants 'one face from your friend group' and messaged you first. Your best friend fits better.

outcomes.text: Your friend gets it and shouts you out in every interview. You're 'the friend.' It's a nice title.

later.text: Remember giving your friend the sneaker deal? They got their own colorway. The launch party is half in your name.

options.label: Take it, say nothing
options.cost: A group chat that finds out

outcomes.text: You take it. C$2,500. The brand posts 'we asked the whole friend group!' Your best friend reads it.

later.text: Remember the sneaker deal? The group chat renamed itself, without you in it. Brunch is cancelled indefinitely.

outcomes.text: They take you both. Half the money, double the fun.
They take neither and hire a model. At least you're even.

title: On air at Real Clout FM, the host asks about Brock Squarejaw's new movie. It's terrible. Brock is listening.

outcomes.text: 'A masterpiece.' Brock's team DMs you set passes and C$1,500 for a cameo.
'A masterpiece.' The movie flops. Your clip becomes the movie's meme.
'Brock tries so hard, and it's so bad.' Listeners love it. The station wants you back weekly.
'It's bad.' Brock's fans flood your posts with his abs. For days.
'The popcorn was elite.' Nobody's upset. Nobody remembers.

title: Lunaria's label wants a 'spontaneous' crying reaction to her new album, filmed before you've heard it.

outcomes.text: You cry beautifully at a song you haven't heard. Lunaria reposts it. C$1,800.

later.text: Remember crying at Lunaria's album? A fan noticed you sobbed at track 4 before it started. Every reaction you ever posted is now 'evidence.'

outcomes.text: You listen. Track 3 genuinely wrecks you. The label posts it anyway, because it's real.
You listen and shrug. The label pays you C$200 to go away.
'I'll cry when I mean it.' The label finds another crier. You find dinner.

title: Lola wants to know who threw a drink at Chardonnay. It was Rudy, from your crew. Front page if you talk.

outcomes.text: Lola runs it: 'a witness tells us.' Your quote is everywhere. So is Rudy's worst selfie.

later.text: Remember naming Rudy? Rudy knows. Rudy told the crew. Rudy is very good at telling the crew.

outcomes.text: 'Didn't see a thing.' Lola sighs. Rudy buys your drinks for a month.
You take it. 'The drink-thrower' turns out to be a brand. Followers pour in.
You take it. Chardonnay's fans flood you for a week. Rudy owes you forever, and he knows it.

later.text: Remember taking the blame for Rudy's drink? Rudy got his first big paycheck. Half of it just landed in your account.

title: Chardonnay Shade's producer wants a juicy secret about your best friend. A good one gets you on the show.

outcomes.text: Your friend's secret airs in episode two. You air in episodes two through nine.

later.text: Remember the secret you sold to Chardonnay's show? Your friend watched episode two. The silence is loud.

outcomes.text: You invent a story about your friend and a goose. They love it. Your friend plays along.
They check. There was no goose. You're cut, and your friend is confused.

options.label: Say no
options.get: A friend who keeps trusting you

outcomes.text: 'Ask someone else.' The producer does. You hear their secret on TV a week later. Not yours to tell, thankfully.

title: Your post is going viral. The joke in it is Jojo's, from the café counter last week. Nobody else knows.

outcomes.text: You add the credit. Jojo's followers jump from 80 to 8,000. She draws free latte art for you forever.

later.text: Remember crediting Jojo? Her open mic tape got her into a sitcom writers' room. She got you a paid punch-up gig.

outcomes.text: It's your joke now. 600,000 likes. Jojo slides your coffee across without the latte art.

later.text: Remember 'your' joke? Jojo's open mic video from last spring surfaced. Same joke. Same pause.
later.headline: BREAKING: a barista's open mic tape shows {name}'s viral joke was hers first. Same punchline, same pause. We reached out. The barista said 'lol.'

outcomes.text: 'My barista said this 💀' pinned. It's technically true. Jojo calls it 'technically true.'

title: At the campus open mic, a magazine editor is listening. The poem you're about to read as yours is your TA's.

outcomes.text: Standing ovation. The editor wants it: C$800 and a page in print.

later.text: Remember 'your' poem? The magazine printed it. Your TA reads that magazine. So does the dean.

options.label: Read it, credit her
options.get: A good night, a grateful TA

outcomes.text: 'This is my TA's.' People clap anyway. The TA hears about it and offers you a paid research job.
You read your own messy poem. Someone cries. It's you. Then others.
You read your own poem. A guy in the back yawns into the mic.

title: An anonymous gossip account wants a source to say your rival Tiff faked her charity trip. It isn't true.

outcomes.text: The post runs. Tiff's brand deals pause. Two of them call you instead.

later.text: Remember the post about Tiff? The account got hacked. Every source is public now, including you.
later.headline: BREAKING: a gossip account's hacked inbox shows {name} fed it a false story about a rival. We reached out. They're 'taking time offline.'

outcomes.text: Tiff gets ahead of it with receipts. The account looks foolish. Tiff owes you one.

later.text: Remember warning Tiff? She landed the brand deal and asked them to bring you in too.

outcomes.text: You say no. Someone else says yes. The post runs anyway.

title: Your rival at the gym is up for the same sponsor. A guy offers 'proof' he's on something. It's photoshopped.

outcomes.text: Your rival is dropped. The sponsor calls you: C$2,500 and a shoot.

later.text: Remember the 'proof'? The original photo turned up. Nothing in it but a protein shake. The gym wants your keycard back.

outcomes.text: You train like a maniac and win the spot. You can't walk, but you won.
You train like a maniac. He still wins. He spots you anyway.

options.label: Tell your rival about the fake

outcomes.text: He reports the guy. The gym bans the faker. Your rival says 'you're good people' and means it.

title: Dolores trained you behind the bar. Marcos offers you her job if you confirm she comps friends. She does.

outcomes.text: Dolores is out. You're in. C$2,000. The regulars ask where Dolores went, every night.

later.text: Remember taking Dolores's job? She opened her own bar across the street. Your regulars followed her.

outcomes.text: 'Never noticed.' Marcos sighs. Dolores slides you a drink: 'I heard.'

later.text: Remember covering for Dolores? She opened her own bar and made you a partner.

options.label: Tell Dolores to stop
options.get: Both of you keep your jobs

outcomes.text: Dolores stops comping. Marcos forgets about it. Nobody loses a job.
Dolores stops, then works out how you knew. 'Who asked you?' Awkward month.

title: Chase Clout's team offers you a mic if you trash Pixel's tournament on stream. Pixel gave you your start.

options.label: Trash the tournament
options.cost: Pixel, who gave you a mic first

outcomes.text: You call it 'a basement LAN party.' Chase's team hires you. Pixel watches the clip twice.

later.text: Remember trashing Pixel's tournament? Chase got banned (again). His team dropped you the same day. Pixel's door is closed.

outcomes.text: 'Not for me.' Pixel hears about it, somehow. He gives you the mic for the finals.
You praise Pixel's tournament on Chase's stream. Chat loves it. Chase's team is furious, then hires you anyway.
You go off script. The stream cuts you off mid-sentence.

title: Peyton Pastel's charity stream wants pledges. Say a big number on camera and your face is on the thank-you.

options.label: Give C$500, for real
options.get: A spot on the thank-you list

outcomes.text: C$500 sent. Peyton reads your name between two celebrities. Small, but it's there.
'C$3,000 from…' Peyton gasps. Your name trends. Nobody checks. Yet.

later.text: Remember the C$3,000 pledge? The charity posted who actually paid. Your name was missing, and someone circled it.
later.headline: Developing: a kids' charity's donor list shows {name} pledged C$3,000 on Peyton Pastel's stream and paid C$0. Peyton has filmed an apology. For them.

outcomes.text: You watch. Tiff pledges C$12. Tiff gets a shoutout.

title: Brick Tackleton's charity day at Meteor Park: pose with the kids for photos, or stay and coach all afternoon.

outcomes.text: Great photos. You're gone by 2. A kid asks Brick where 'the photo person' went.

later.text: Remember the charity day photos? A parent posted you leaving at 2:03, still waving. 'The photo person.'

outcomes.text: You coach all afternoon. Your team loses 14 to 0. Brick hugs you like you won.

later.text: Remember coaching at Brick's charity day? Brick told the story on a late-night show and called you 'the realest one there.'

title: Skyler Beta's startup wants a 'Head of Vibes' with a degree you don't have. The form has a box to tick.

outcomes.text: You're Head of Vibes. C$3,000. You make a playlist and a beanbag plan.

later.text: Remember the degree box? Skyler's investors ran checks before a funding round. You're out. So is the playlist.
later.headline: BREAKING: Skyler Beta's latest startup parts ways with its Head of Vibes, {name}, over a degree that was 'mostly vibes.' The beanbags stay.

options.label: Leave it blank, pitch anyway
options.get: A shot on your own merits

outcomes.text: Skyler hires you anyway: 'Degrees are legacy tech.' C$1,500.
They pass. Skyler says 'love the energy' and ghosts.
The University of Excellence emails it in two hours. You start Monday: C$3,000 minus the C$400.
The University of Excellence is on the news tonight, with its student list. You're on it.

title: Chad Kensington, CEO, wants you as an 'advisor.' You just have to post that you've 'scaled three companies.'

options.label: Post it
options.cost: A lie with your photo on it

outcomes.text: 'Advisor, Stealth Startup.' C$1,500. Chad's domain name now lists you.

later.text: Remember 'scaled three companies'? Someone asked which three. You named three. One is a lemonade stand. The thread has 4,000 replies.

outcomes.text: 'Advisor (learning).' Chad loves it: 'So authentic.' C$600.
You pass. Chad pivots to a new idea before dinner.

title: Dunk Daniels scraped a parked car outside Meteor Park. Before tip-off, he asks you to say you were driving.

outcomes.text: Sgt. Bev takes your statement and three hours of your evening. Dunk sends courtside seats and a signed sneaker.

later.text: Remember taking the fall for Dunk? He called. 'One more tiny favor.'

outcomes.text: 'Own it, man.' Dunk stares, then laughs and leaves the owner his number and a signed ball. 'You're right.'
Dunk shrugs and finds a rookie to say it. You're off his list.
The clip sells for C$2,500: 'DUNK'S DING.' Meteor Park's security knows your face now.

title: Dunk again: hold his bag at the airport while he 'talks to someone.' It's heavy. He's in a hurry.

outcomes.text: It's 200 pairs of sneakers. C$3,000 for your patience.
It's undeclared sneakers. Customs is not amused. Three hours in a back room.
'I'm done, Dunk.' He goes quiet, then says 'respect.' The courtside seats stop. You feel lighter.
'Sneakers I didn't declare.' You walk. He finds someone who doesn't ask.

title: Skyler Beta's app leaked 10,000 users' selfies. His team asks you, intern for a day, to say you did it.

options.label: Say you pushed it
options.cost: Your name on a data leak

outcomes.text: 'Intern error.' C$3,000. Skyler hugs you on stream. The internet learns your name, badly.

later.text: Remember 'intern error'? An investigation found the real button-pusher: Skyler. You lied for him, on the record.
later.headline: Developing: an investigation into Skyler Beta's selfie leak finds {name} was paid to take the blame. Skyler, reached for comment: 'We're pivoting.'

outcomes.text: 'No.' Skyler calls you 'not a team player' on a podcast. Twelve people hear it.

options.label: Tell Lola who really did it
options.cost: Every startup on the gig board

outcomes.text: Lola runs it. Skyler's investors call him. The startups on the gig board quietly stop hiring you.
